title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཐེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 179)
shelf_note: Authentic Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa (epistemology/logic) volume leaf (vol. The / 179).

ocr_errors.problem: Apparatus variant curly braces notation in transcription where woodblock image reads བརྫུན

tr_errors_A.english: the two means of realization <note>the arguments or perspectives of the two disputants</note> will conflict. If other means of realization are required to resolve this, it leads to an infinite regress
tr_errors_A.problem: Technical term rtogs byed (debate arbiters / evaluators) mistranslated as 'means of realization' and glossed as the disputants' perspectives, obscuring the third-party arbiter regress argument

tr_errors_A.english: When those who provide the means of realization—the proponent and the opponent—have differing intellects
tr_errors_A.problem: Conflates the arbiters (rtogs par byed pa rnams) with the disputing parties (rgol ba dang phyir rgol ba), merging distinct entities in the debate structure

tr_errors_A.english: because this [new realization] which comes from the power of valid cognition does not harm the previous one
tr_errors_A.problem: Reverses the meaning of the epistemological argument: valid cognition overturns previous erroneous claims rather than leaving them unharmed

tr_errors_A.english: how can you speak of all desires being non-existent or incomplete?
tr_errors_A.problem: Technical term 'dod (asserted thesis / position, Skt. iṣṭa) mistranslated as psychological 'desires'
The hanging catchword at the bottom-right edge of the folio leaf is omitted

tr_errors_B.english: Thus, in whatever manner a previous acceptance might be harmed by this, it is not harmed by what arrives through the force of valid cognition
tr_errors_B.problem: Confuses the subject-object direction of invalidation (gnod pa) between the prior claim and valid cognition

tr_errors_B.english: how could one speak of the non-existence of everything that is desired, or of incompleteness and the like?
tr_errors_B.problem: Translates 'dod (accepted thesis / assertion, Skt. iṣṭa) literally as 'desired' rather than accepted position

pages.prefer_reason: Translation B correctly identifies 'rtogs byed' as debate arbiters, maintains the structural distinction between judges and disputants, and preserves the page catchword, whereas Translation A misidentifies the arbiters and reverses an epistemological claim regarding valid cognition.

book_verdict: Authentic Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa folio with a clean woodblock image, virtually flawless OCR transcription, and sound philosophical debate content on epistemic arbitration and Madhyamaka emptiness.
